h1: Kanya Place Maha Sarakham — A Quiet Little Boutique in Town With Private Balconies at a Friendly Price
intro: If you are in Maha Sarakham on business, or visiting a son or daughter studying at the university, and you want a quiet, clean place in town within walking distance of the market and restaurants — Kanya Place is a small boutique hotel locals speak well of. It sits in a lane in the Talat area on Chaloem Phrakiat Rama IX Road, with rooms that have private balconies, AC, TV, free Wi-Fi and free parking. It scores 8.3 from 78 reviews and starts at around ฿650/night.

body.html: Kanya Place is the kind of stay locals call a "place" — a boutique hotel of just a handful of rooms, owner-run rather than part of a big chain. The thing guests love most is that every room has its own private balcony, which is rare at this price in Maha Sarakham. You can step out for a morning coffee and look down a quiet lane in peace.

The rooms themselves are simple but well kept — cool AC, a comfy bed, a flat-screen TV, a work desk, a wardrobe and an en-suite bathroom with a hot shower. The thing guests praise most is cleanliness: review after review mentions tidy rooms, fresh linens and daily housekeeping. Wi-Fi reaches throughout, there is free parking out front, and a small minimart for essentials.
"Very clean room, the staff greeted me warmly and looked after us well, the lane is quiet so we slept soundly. We'll definitely stay again next time."

The location works well for anyone coming into town — it is about 880 metres from the centre, so you can walk to the market and local restaurants, with 7-Eleven, massage shops, coffee places and food stalls nearby. Mahasarakham University and the Taksila landmark are a short drive away. It suits people with a car or who are happy to call a ride, since local public transport is still limited.

Staff are another high point — warm, friendly and helpful. The main gripe is that, because the hotel is small, it can be hard to book during the university's graduation week or exam periods, when the few rooms fill fast. If you are coming then, book several weeks ahead.

To be straight with you: Kanya Place carries a 4-star tag on the platforms, but in reality it is a small budget boutique, not a full-service hotel with a big lobby, a pool or an on-site restaurant. There is no breakfast served, so you head out to eat (easy enough in this area). If you expect big-hotel service you may be let down, but if you want a clean, quiet room with a balcony at a fair price, it delivers above what you pay.

In short, Kanya Place suits short business trips, visiting relatives who study here, or parents dropping a child at their dorm. You get a clean, quiet room with a balcony to sit on and free parking, all at an easy price. The 8.3 score from more than 78 reviews reflects guests who mostly leave happy — and plenty who say they would come back.

honestSummary: Kanya Place is a small boutique that does the basics better than its price suggests — clean, quiet rooms with balconies, in town, with free parking. Just understand it is not a full-service hotel: no breakfast, no pool, and the few rooms get hard to book at peak times.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Kanya Place Maha Sarakham

faq.q: Where is Kanya Place in Maha Sarakham, and is it easy to get around?
faq.a: Kanya Place is at 128/1 Chaloem Phrakiat Rama IX Road in the Talat area, central Maha Sarakham, about 880 metres from the centre — walkable to the market and restaurants. It has free parking, so it is easy with a car. Without one, budget for ride-hailing, as local public transport is still limited.

faq.q: How much is Kanya Place and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿650/night for a Standard double. There are also Twin and larger Deluxe rooms for a little more. Every room has a private balcony, AC, TV and free Wi-Fi. Prices vary by season, so compare a few platforms before you book.

faq.q: Who is Kanya Place best for?
faq.a: It suits short business trips, visiting relatives who study at the university, or parents dropping a child at their dorm. You get a clean, quiet room with a balcony and free parking at a fair price. It is not for travellers who want a big hotel with a pool or on-site breakfast.

faq.q: Does Kanya Place have breakfast and a pool?
faq.a: No breakfast and no pool — it is a small boutique. But there are food stalls, coffee shops and a 7-Eleven within walking distance, so eating out in the morning is easy. The hotel does have a small minimart for essentials.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: Usually one to two weeks is enough. But during Mahasarakham University graduation and exam weeks the few rooms fill very fast — for those dates, book several weeks ahead and choose a free-cancellation rate to be safe.
